newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: GOLD-Cerro Vanguardia to mine Patagonia in 1998.
newsitem.headline: GOLD-Cerro Vanguardia to mine Patagonia in 1998.

text.p: Cerro Vanguardia, the $230-million gold project approved in Patagonia by Minorco SA and Argentina's Perez Companc, should produce its first dore gold bars by mid-1998, the company said.

Cerro Vanguardia will produce an average six tonnes of gold and 60 tonnes of silver a year during its estimated mine-life of 15 years, in the form of the dore bars containing 90 percent silver and 10 percent gold.

Luxembourg-based Minorco --the offshore arm of South Africa's Anglo American Corp -- and Perez Companc exercized an option to exploit the site in far southern Argentina in late December. They are now negotiating with refiners and seeking financing.
Financing for the open-pit, vetiform gold operation should be ready in "six to eight months, what it usually takes," Cerro Vanguardia President Josef Oppenheimer told Reuters in an interview.

Minorco, operating then as Anglo-American, formed an Argentine mining joint venture, Mincorp, with Perez Companc in 1988. The two companies had previously been associated in the oil and petrochemical business in Argentina.

Minorco's presence in Argentina dates back to 1980 and it has examined properties throughout the country. One of the prospects it examined was Bajo de la Alumbrera, now a billion-dollar copper project being led by Australia's MIM Holdings, but Minorco could not reach an agreement with the provincial government.
"We still own mining rights in the northern provinces but nothing that we believe has the potential to justify further work," Oppenheimer said.

Apart from exploring to expand Cerro Vanguardia's reserves, Mincorp is also looking in other parts of Patagonia. But for the moment the company feels it has taken on enough of a financial load by developing Cerro Vanguardia.

"We are quite happy with (Cerro Vanguardia). It has taken enough resources for us to concentrate on that. We want to do this one right," Oppenheimer said. But he added, "Our exploration in the area will continue in the areas which we have explored, the general Patagonian area."
While Mincorp has identified other vetiform gold formations in the zone, it is possible that it has already found the best deposit, according to Oppenheimer.
"The opinion of some geologists is that Cerro Vanguardia is the filet mignon of the area and that all the rest is not going to be as good. We have other claims but nothing so far that size," he said.
Cerro Vanguardia has triggered a minor gold rush in Patagonia, with a clutch of foreign companies being lured to to see if they can find something similar.
Oppenheimer declined to say how advanced Mincorp's work on other claims in the area was or how much they were spending on Argentine exploration outside Cerro Vanguardia.
Exploration at the Cerro Vanguardia site is also examining the possibility of developing an underground operation and possibly heap-leaching lower grade material.
Another option Cerro Vanguardia is studying is that of installing its own refinery, but Oppenheimer said it did not look likely to go ahead.
"I don't think that it will be a good proposition. The tonnage is so small," he said.
Minorco and Perez Companc each hold 46.25 percent of Cerro Vanguardia, while the site's owner Fomicruz, a company belonging to the government of Santa Cruz province, has the remaining 7.5 percent.
